text:
<meta>continues from previous page: Li Ru urged Dong Zhuo to appoint famous scholars to win public favor. Dong followed this advice and recommended Cai Yong for his talent. Dong ordered him to report for duty.</meta>

Cai Yong refused at first. Dong Zhuo was furious and sent a messenger to tell Cai, "If you do not come, I will exterminate your clan." Fearing for his life, Cai Yong had no choice but to obey the order and arrive. Dong Zhuo was overjoyed to see him and promoted him three times in one month, eventually appointing him as a Palace Attendant, treating him with great closeness and favor. <gloss>Always relying on the patronage of the powerful as Wang Feng and Yang Xiong did. Fearing one's own body might end up as firewood, or buried by a woodcutter on Mount Kun.</gloss>

Meanwhile, the Young Emperor, Empress Dowager He, and Lady Tang were trapped in the Yong'an Palace. Their clothing and food were gradually running low, and the Young Emperor’s tears never dried. <gloss>As the later king said, the days and months spent here are difficult.</gloss> One day, he happened to see a pair of swallows flying in the courtyard and recited a poem. <gloss>In the empty courtyard, birds fly and dance; in this cold palace and abandoned temple, I am alone, and my years are my own.</gloss>

The poem went:

Tender grass, green and dense with mist,
The pair of swallows fly with grace.
The Luo River, a single ribbon of blue,
People on the road admire its charm.
<gloss>The first half of the poem sings of the swallows and gazes into the distance.</gloss>
Deep within the blue clouds lies the palace where I once lived.
<gloss>Gazing until the eyes ache at the old palace, unable to fly there; truly, I am not as fortunate as the pair of swallows that can return to their old nest. How tragic.</gloss>
Who will act with loyalty and righteousness,
And vent the resentment in my heart?
<gloss>The second half is a poem of personal desire. The poem is well-written.</gloss>

Dong Zhuo often sent people to spy on them. That day, his agents intercepted this poem and presented it to him. Dong Zhuo said, "He is full of resentment and writes poetry. There is sufficient cause to kill him." <gloss>There is a famous precedent for killing him to teach the world a lesson.</gloss> He then ordered Li Ru to lead eighteen armed guards into the palace to murder the Emperor. The Emperor, the Empress Dowager, and Lady Tang were sitting on the upper floor when a palace maid reported that Li Ru had arrived. The Emperor was terrified. Li Ru presented a cup of poisoned wine to the Emperor. <gloss>It is ironic that this poem, which mentions drinking, would meet its end through this very act of drinking, which is usually a refined affair.</gloss>

<summary>Li Ru pressures the scholar Cai Yong into serving Dong Zhuo, while the imprisoned Young Emperor expresses his despair through poetry, leading Dong Zhuo to order his assassination via poison.</summary>
<keywords>Li Ru, Dong Zhuo, Cai Yong, Young Emperor, Empress Dowager He, Lady Tang, assassination, regicide, poisoned wine</keywords>
